## Administration

Main article: [Administration of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administration_of_Paris)

### City government

Further information: [Arrondissements of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Paris)
See also: [Mayor of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Paris)A map of the [arrondissements of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissements_of_Paris)
For almost all of its long history, except for a few brief periods, Paris was governed directly by representatives of the king, emperor, or president of France. In 1974, Paris was granted municipal autonomy by the National Assembly.[[109]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFierro1996334-112) The first modern elected mayor of Paris was [Jacques Chirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Chirac), elected in March 1977, becoming the city's first mayor since 1871 and only the fourth since 1794. The current mayor is [Emmanuel Grégoire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Grégoire), a member of the [Socialist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_(France)), who was elected in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Paris_municipal_election).[[110]](#cite_note-113)The [Hôtel de Ville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hôtel_de_Ville,_Paris), or city hall
The mayor of Paris is [elected indirectly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indirect_election) by Paris voters. The voters of each of the city's 20 arrondissements elect members to the [Conseil de Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conseil_de_Paris) (Council of Paris), which elects the mayor. The council is composed of 163 members. Each arrondissement is allocated many seats, dependent upon its population, from 10 members for each of the least-populated arrondissements to 34 members for the most populated. The council is elected using [closed list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed_list) [proportional representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proportional_representation) in a [two-round system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-round_system).[[111]](#cite_note-Election_Code_–_Article_L260-114)
Party lists winning an absolute [majority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majority) in the first round – or at least a [plurality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plurality_(voting)) in the second round – automatically win half the seats of an arrondissement. The remaining half of the seats are distributed proportionally to all lists which win at least 5% of the vote, using the [highest averages method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highest_averages_method).[[111]](#cite_note-Election_Code_–_Article_L260-114) This ensures that the winning party or coalition always wins a majority of the seats, even if they do not win an absolute majority of the vote.[[112]](#cite_note-Pariscouncil-115)
Before the [2020 Paris municipal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Paris_municipal_election), each of Paris's 20 arrondissements had its own town hall and a directly elected council ([conseil d'arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conseil_d'arrondissement)), which elects an arrondissement mayor.[[113]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShales200716-116) The council of each arrondissement is composed of members of the Conseil de Paris, and members who serve only on the council of the arrondissement. The number of deputy mayors in each arrondissement varies depending on its population. As of 1996, there were 20 arrondissement mayors and 120 deputy mayors.[[109]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFierro1996334-112) The creation of [Paris Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Centre), a unified administrative division with a single mayor covering the first four arrondissements, took effect with the said 2020 election. The other 16 arrondissements continue to have their own mayors.[[114]](#cite_note-117)

### Métropole du Grand Paris
A map of the Greater Paris Metropolis and its governing territories
In January 2016, the [Métropole du Grand Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Paris) came into existence.[[115]](#cite_note-MGP-118) It is an administrative structure for co-operation between the City of Paris and its nearest suburbs. It includes the City of Paris, plus the communes of the three departments of the inner suburbs, [Hauts-de-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hauts-de-Seine), [Seine-Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-Saint-Denis) and [Val-de-Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-de-Marne), plus seven communes in the outer suburbs, including [Argenteuil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argenteuil) in [Val d'Oise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val_d'Oise) and [Paray-Vieille-Poste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paray-Vieille-Poste) in [Essonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essonne), which were added to include the major airports of Paris. The Metropole covers 814 km2 (314 sq mi). In 2015, it had a population of 6.945 million people.[[116]](#cite_note-119)[[117]](#cite_note-lemoniteur1-120)
The new structure is administered by a Metropolitan Council of 210 members, not directly elected, but chosen by the councils of the member Communes. By 2020, its basic competencies will include urban planning, housing, and protection of the environment.[[115]](#cite_note-MGP-118)[[117]](#cite_note-lemoniteur1-120) In January 2016, [Patrick Ollier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ollier) was elected the first president of the metropolitan council. Though the Metropole has a population of nearly seven million people and accounts for 25 percent of the GDP of France, it has a very small budget: just 65 million Euros, compared with eight billion Euros for the City of Paris.[[118]](#cite_note-121)

### Regional government

The [Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Region) of [Île de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île_de_France), including Paris and its surrounding communities, is governed by the [Regional Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Council_of_Île-de-France), composed of 209 members representing the different communes. In December 2015, a list of candidates of the Union of the Right, a coalition of centrist and right-wing parties, led by [Valérie Pécresse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valérie_Pécresse), narrowly won the regional election, defeating a coalition of Socialists and ecologists. The Socialists had governed the region for seventeen years. The regional council has 121 members from the Union of the Right, 66 from the Union of the Left and 22 from the extreme right National Front.[[119]](#cite_note-122)

### National government
The [Élysée Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Élysée_Palace), official residence of the [President of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France)
As the capital of France, Paris is the seat of France's [national government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_France). For the executive, the two chief officers each have their own official residences, which also serve as their offices. The [President of the French Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France) resides at the [Élysée Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Élysée_Palace).[[120]](#cite_note-123) The [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_France)'s seat is at the [Hôtel Matignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hôtel_Matignon).[[121]](#cite_note-124)[[122]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKnappWright200693–94-125) Government ministries are located in various parts of the city, many near the Hôtel Matignon.[[123]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBorrus2012288-126)
Both houses of the [French Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Parliament) are located on the Rive Gauche. The upper house, the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_(France)), meets in the [Palais du Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_du_Luxembourg). The more important lower house, the [National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_(France)), meets in the [Palais Bourbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_Bourbon). The [President of the Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_Senate_of_France), the second-highest public official in France, with the President of the Republic being the sole superior, resides in the [Petit Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petit_Luxembourg), a smaller palace annexe to the Palais du Luxembourg.[[124]](#cite_note-127)The Palais-Royal, residence of the [Conseil d'État](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conseil_d'État_(France))
France's highest courts are located in Paris. The [Court of Cassation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Cassation_(France)), the highest court in the judicial order, which reviews criminal and civil cases, is located in the [Palais de Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_de_Justice,_Paris) on the Île de la Cité.[[125]](#cite_note-128) The [Conseil d'État](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_State_(France)), which provides legal advice to the executive and acts as the highest court in the administrative order, judging litigation against public bodies, is located in the [Palais-Royal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais-Royal) in the [1st arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_arrondissement_of_Paris).[[126]](#cite_note-129) The [Constitutional Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Council_of_France), an advisory body with ultimate authority on the constitutionality of laws and government decrees, meets in the Montpensier wing of the Palais Royal.[[127]](#cite_note-130)
Paris and its region host the headquarters of several international organisations, including [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO), the [Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development), the [International Chamber of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Chamber_of_Commerce), the [Paris Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Club), the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency), the [International Energy Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Energy_Agency), the [Organisation internationale de la Francophonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_internationale_de_la_Francophonie), the [European Union Institute for Security Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union_Institute_for_Security_Studies), the [International Bureau of Weights and Measures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bureau_of_Weights_and_Measures), the [International Exhibition Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_International_Expositions), and the [International Federation for Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_for_Human_Rights).

### Police force
[Gendarmerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Gendarmerie) motorcyclists
The security of Paris is mainly the responsibility of the [Prefecture of Police of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefecture_of_Police_of_Paris), a subdivision of the [Ministry of the Interior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_the_Interior_(France)). It supervises the units of the [National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Police_(France)) who patrol the city and the three neighbouring departments. It is also responsible for providing emergency services, including the [Paris Fire Brigade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Fire_Brigade). Its headquarters is on [Place Louis Lépine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_Louis_Lépine) on the [Île de la Cité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île_de_la_Cité).[[128]](#cite_note-Presentation_Generale-131)
There are 43,800 officers under the prefecture, and a fleet of more than 6,000 vehicles, including police cars, motorcycles, fire trucks, boats, and helicopters.[[128]](#cite_note-Presentation_Generale-131) The national police has its own special unit for riot control and crowd control, and security of public buildings, called the [Compagnies Républicaines de Sécurité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compagnies_Républicaines_de_Sécurité) (CRS). Vans of CRS agents are frequently seen in the centre of Paris when there are demonstrations and public events. The police are supported by the [National Gendarmerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Gendarmerie), a branch of the [French Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Armed_Forces). Their police operations are supervised by the [Ministry of the Interior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interior_ministry).[[129]](#cite_note-132)
Crime in Paris is similar to that in most large cities. Violent crime is relatively rare in the city centre. Political violence is uncommon, though very large demonstrations may occur in Paris and other French cities simultaneously. These demonstrations, usually managed by a strong police presence, can turn confrontational and escalate into violence.[[130]](#cite_note-133)

## Cityscape

A panorama of Paris from the Eiffel Tower, in a 360-degree view. The [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine) river flows from the north-east to the south-west, right to left

### Urbanism and architecture

See also: [Architecture of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Architecture_of_Paris), [Haussmann's renovation of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haussmann's_renovation_of_Paris), [Religious buildings in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_buildings_in_Paris), and [List of tallest buildings in the Paris region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_the_Paris_region)The [Rue de Rivoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rue_de_Rivoli)The [Place des Vosges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_des_Vosges), the oldest planned square in Paris
Paris is one of the few world capitals that has rarely seen destruction by catastrophe or war. As a result, even its earliest history is visible in its street map, and centuries of rulers adding their respective architectural marks on the capital have resulted in an accumulated wealth of history-rich monuments and buildings whose beauty plays a large part in giving Paris the reputation it has today.[[131]](#cite_note-134) At its origin, before the Middle Ages, Paris was composed of several islands and sandbanks in a bend of the [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine). Of those, two remain today: [Île Saint-Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île_Saint-Louis) and the [Île de la Cité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île_de_la_Cité). A third one is the 1827 artificially created [Île aux Cygnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île_aux_Cygnes).
Modern Paris owes much of its downtown plan and architectural harmony to [Napoleon III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon_III) and his Prefect of the Seine, [Baron Haussmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georges-Eugène_Haussmann). Between [1853 and 1870 they rebuilt the city centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haussmann's_renovation_of_Paris), created the wide downtown boulevards and squares where the boulevards intersected, imposed standard facades along the boulevards, and required that the facades be built of the distinctive cream-grey "[Paris stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_stone)". They built the major parks around central Paris.[[132]](#cite_note-135) The high residential population of the city centre makes Paris much different from most other major western cities.[[133]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBraimohVlek200812-136)
Paris's urbanism laws have been under strict control since the early 17th century,[[134]](#cite_note-plan_hauteurs-137) particularly where street-front alignment, building height and building distribution is concerned.[[134]](#cite_note-plan_hauteurs-137) The 210 m (690 ft) [Tour Montparnasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_Montparnasse) was both Paris's and France's tallest building from 1973 until 2011,[[135]](#cite_note-138) when the record was taken by the [La Défense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Défense) district's [Tour First](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_First) in the commune of [Courbevoie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courbevoie).

### Housing
[Front de Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_de_Seine) development along the river [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine)
In 2018, the most expensive residential street in Paris by average price per square metre was [Avenue Montaigne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avenue_Montaigne), at 22,372 euros per square metre.[[136]](#cite_note-139) In 2011, the number of residences in the City of Paris was 1,356,074. Among these, 1,165,541 (85.9 percent) were main residences, 91,835 (6.8 percent) were secondary residences, and the remaining 7.3 percent were empty.[[137]](#cite_note-insee_logement-140)
Sixty-two percent of buildings date from 1949 and before, with 20 percent built between 1949 and 1974. 18 percent of Paris buildings were built after 1974.[[138]](#cite_note-notaires_idf-141) Two-thirds of the city's 1.3 million residences are studio and two-room apartments. Paris averages 1.9 people per residence, a number that has remained constant since the 1980s, which is less than Île-de-France's 2.33 people-per-residence average. Only 33 percent of Parisian principal residents own their habitation, against 47 percent for the wider [Île-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île-de-France) region. Most of Paris's population rents their residence.[[138]](#cite_note-notaires_idf-141) In 2017, social or public housing was 19.9 percent of Paris's residences. #
Insee Flash Ile-de-France ·
               Avril 2026 · n° 111L’Île-de-France conserve un solde naturel largement excédentaire Bilan démographique 2025

François Dubujet (Insee)

Au 1er janvier 2026, l’Île-de-France compte 12,59 millions d’habitants. Avec 148 300 naissances
               en 2025, la baisse de la natalité se poursuit dans la région et elle est plus marquée
               qu’au niveau national. Le nombre de décès est stable en 2025, à 79 300. Bien que toujours
               largement positif, l’excédent naturel francilien se réduit à nouveau (+69 000), prolongeant
               ainsi la tendance entamée en 2015. Il demeure néanmoins le moteur de la croissance
               démographique francilienne et l’Île-de-France est, avec Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, l’une
               des deux seules régions métropolitaines conservant un excédent naturel.
Contrairement aux années précédentes, la fécondité recule autant en Île-de-France
               que dans le reste de la France, avec un indicateur conjoncturel de fécondité à 1,63
               contre 1,56 au niveau national.
L’espérance de vie à la naissance progresse à nouveau en 2025 (+0,1 an) : elle atteint
               86,5 ans pour les femmes et 82,0 ans pour les hommes.

## 12,59 millions d’habitants au 1er janvier 2026

Au 1er janvier 2026, la population de l’Île-de-France est estimée à 12 594 500 habitants
                     ([figure 1](#figure1)). Au cours de l’année 2025, la population augmente de 45 200 habitants, soit une
                     progression de 0,36 %. Cette hausse est un peu inférieure à la moyenne annuelle constatée
                     au cours des cinq dernières années (+0,45 %).
Au cours de l’année 2025, la population progresse dans tous les départements de la
                     région, à l’exception de Paris (-18 000 habitants) qui perd régulièrement des habitants
                     depuis 2012. Comme les trois années précédentes, les hausses de population sont les
                     plus fortes en Seine-Saint-Denis et en Seine-et-Marne (respectivement +13 900 et +11 200
                     habitants).

## La croissance francilienne toujours portée par l’excédent naturel

La croissance de la population francilienne est entièrement portée par le solde naturel. Toutefois, compte tenu de la baisse du nombre de naissances et du maintien du nombre
                     de décès en 2025 par rapport à 2024, l’excédent naturel régional recule légèrement
                     mais reste largement positif, passant de 73 200 habitants en 2024 à 69 000 en 2025
                     ([figure 2](#figure2)). Quant au déficit migratoire, il reste important, mais s’amenuise (de -31 400 en 2024 à -23 800 en 2025). La réduction
                     simultanée de l’excédent naturel et du déficit migratoire explique le maintien de
                     la croissance démographique dans la région.
L’Île-de-France est, avec la région Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, l’une des deux régions métropolitaines
                     où le solde naturel est positif en 2025. Néanmoins, celui d’Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes est
                     bien plus faible qu’en Île-de-France. En comparaison, le solde naturel devient négatif
                     dans les Hauts-de-France et le déficit naturel se creuse dans toutes les autres régions
                     de France métropolitaine.
En 2025, 148 300 bébés sont nés en Île-de-France, soit 4 250 de moins qu’en 2024 (-2,8 %).
                     Ce recul s’inscrit dans une baisse tandancielle. L’année 2025 est la onzième année
                     consécutive de réduction du nombre de naissances dans la région, et cette baisse est
                     plus prononcée que celle de 2024 (-1,0 %). Contrairement aux deux années précédentes,
                     elle est aussi un peu plus marquée en Île-de-France qu’en moyenne sur l’ensemble du
                     territoire national (-2,4 % en 2025). Depuis le point haut atteint en 2010, le recul
                     des naissances atteint 19,6 %, soit à peine moins que celui enregistré au niveau national
                     (-23,8 %).
La baisse continue des naissances se traduit par une diminution de la population des
                     jeunes enfants, phénomène accentué par un solde migratoire négatif à ces âges. Ainsi,
                     au 1er janvier 2026, les personnes de moins de 20 ans représentent 23,7 % de la population,
                     contre 25,3 % en 2021. À l’inverse, en haut de la pyramide des âges, le vieillissement
                     des baby-boomers accroît la proportion des seniors, qui atteint 16,7 % (contre 15,4 %
                     en 2020). De ce fait, l’indice de jeunesse, représentant le nombre de personnes de
                     moins de 20 ans pour 100 personnes de 65 ans ou plus, continue de diminuer fortement,
                     passant de 205 en 2010 à 166 en 2020 et 142 en 2026. Néanmoins, une baisse est enregistrée
                     également dans les autres régions de France métropolitaine, de sorte que le ratio
                     francilien reste le plus élevé.

## La fécondité recule autant en Île-de-France qu’au niveau national

En 2025, en Île-de-France, l’indicateur conjoncturel de fécondité (ICF) s’établit à 1,63 enfant par femme, un niveau inférieur à celui observé en 2024
                     (1,68). La baisse de l’ICF s’amplifie : elle était plus modérée l’année précédente,
                     passant de 1,71 en 2023 à 1,68 en 2024. L’ICF régional atteint ainsi un niveau historiquement
                     bas, inférieur aux niveaux faibles atteints en 1976 (1,72) et en 1994 (1,74), et s’éloigne
                     encore un peu plus du seuil de renouvellement des générations (2,05 enfants par femme). Le niveau de fécondité demeure toutefois relativement élevé
                     en Île-de-France au regard du niveau national, qui recule à 1,56 en 2025. L’écart
                     entre l’indicateur régional et l’indicateur national se maintient, traduisant une
                     baisse similaire à la moyenne nationale alors que, les années précédentes, l’Île-de-France
                     résistait un peu mieux au recul de la fécondité que la plupart des autres régions
                     métropolitaines.
L’évolution du nombre de naissances dépend à la fois du nombre de femmes en âge de
                     procréer et de leur fécondité. La population féminine de 20 à 40 ans, âges où les
                     femmes sont les plus fécondes, progresse lentement depuis 2020 pour retrouver son
                     niveau du début des années 1990. Le recul du nombre des naissances en Île-de-France
                     au cours des six dernières années s’explique donc uniquement par celui de la fécondité,
                     c’est-à-dire du nombre d’enfants par femme.
En 2025, l’ICF est une nouvelle fois au-dessous du seuil de renouvellement des générations
                     dans tous les départements de l’Île-de-France. Il se maintient à un niveau encore
                     élevé dans le Val-d’Oise (1,94) et en Seine-Saint-Denis (1,92). À Paris, le niveau
                     de l’ICF (1,26) reste l’un des plus bas des départements de France métropolitaine,
                     seulement supérieur à celui observé dans les deux départements corses (1,13). Cela
                     tient notamment à une maternité nettement plus tardive que dans les autres départements.
                     Depuis 2020, l’ICF des femmes parisiennes âgées de 35 à 49 ans est supérieur à celui
                     de celles âgées de 25 à 34 ans (respectivement 0,65 et 0,56 en 2025). Même si le recul
                     de l’âge à la maternité est une tendance générale, l’ICF des femmes de 35 à 49 ans
                     reste inférieur à celui des femmes de 25 à 34 ans, dans les autres départements franciliens
                     et au niveau régional (respectivement 0,58 et 0,93 en 2025).
Ainsi, en 2025, l’âge conjoncturel moyen à l’accouchement est de 34,6 ans à Paris, le plus élevé de la région. En Île-de-France, cet âge moyen
                     s’établit à 32,5 ans, soit un an de plus qu’en 2015 et cinq ans de plus qu’en 1981.
                     C’est le niveau le plus élevé de toutes les régions de France métropolitaine (31,2 ans
                     en moyenne).

## Une stabilité des décès et une reprise des gains d’espérance de vie

En 2025, 79 300 personnes sont décédées en Île-de-France, soit un nombre équivalent
                     à celui de 2024 (79 400). Cette relative stagnation est une caractéristique commune
                     avec la Nouvelle-Aquitaine, tandis que le nombre de décès augmente dans toutes les
                     autres régions et en France métropolitaine (+1,0 %).
Au sein de la région, l’évolution de la mortalité est très variable d’un département
                     à l’autre. Le nombre de décès diminue à Paris, en petite couronne et dans l’Essonne,
                     mais augmente dans les trois autres départements de grande couronne.
Le vieillissement de la population, avec une part croissante de personnes atteignant
                     les âges où la mortalité est plus élevée, touche tous les départements d’Île-de-France
                     comme l’ensemble de la France. À Paris, la part de la population âgée d’au moins 80 ans
                     atteint 5,3 %, un point de plus que la moyenne régionale. Ce vieillissement de la
                     population concourt à accroître la mortalité. Néanmoins, en 2025, l’Île-de-France
                     restant une région relativement jeune, le taux de mortalité y est inférieur de 3 points
                     au taux national (6,3 ‰ contre 9,4 ‰), un écart qui tend à augmenter depuis 30 ans :
                     il n’était que de 1,7 point en 1992 (7,2 ‰ contre 8,9 ‰).
En 2025, en Île-de-France, l’espérance de vie à la naissance est de 86,5 ans pour les femmes (85,9 ans pour la France entière) et de 82,0 ans
                     pour les hommes (80,3 ans au niveau national). Qu’il s’agisse des femmes ou des hommes,
                     le gain d’espérance de vie en 2025 est faible (+0,1 an), en comparaison de l’année
                     2023 où elle avait fortement augmenté par rapport aux trois années précédentes marquées
                     par une forte mortalité liée à l’épidémie de Covid-19. En revanche, ce gain est proche
                     du rythme moyen observé sur la période de 2010 à 2019, soit +0,1 an pour les femmes
                     et +0,2 an pour les hommes.

## Sources

Le recensement de la population sert de base aux [estimations annuelles de population](https://www.insee.fr/fr/metadonnees/source/serie/s1169). Pour les années 2024 et suivantes, les estimations de population sont provisoires :
                        la population du recensement 2023 est actualisée au moyen d’estimations du solde naturel
                        établi à partir des statistiques d’état civil à fin novembre 2025 et du solde migratoire apparent. La population francilienne au
                        1er janvier 2025, estimée fin 2024 à 12 450 900 habitants, a ainsi été révisée fin 2025
                        à 12 549 300 habitants.

## Définitions

Le solde naturel est la différence entre le nombre de naissances et le nombre de décès enregistrés
                           au cours d’une période. S’il est positif, il s’agit d’un excédent naturel, s’il est
                           négatif, d’un déficit naturel.

Le solde migratoire est mesuré indirectement par différence entre, d’une part, l’évolution du niveau
                           de la population entre deux années successives et, d’autre part, le solde naturel.

L’indicateur conjoncturel de fécondité (ICF) est la somme des taux de fécondité par âge observés pour une année donnée.
                           Il peut être interprété comme le nombre moyen d’enfants qu’aurait une génération fictive
                           de femmes qui connaîtraient, tout au long de leur vie féconde, les taux de fécondité
                           par âge observés cette année-là. Il est exprimé en nombre d’enfants par femme. C’est
                           un indicateur synthétique des taux de fécondité par âge de l’année considérée.

Le seuil de renouvellement des générations correspond au nombre moyen d’enfants par femme nécessaire pour que chaque génération
                           en engendre une suivante de même effectif. Il est fixé à 2,05 enfants par femme, parce
                           que pour 100 filles, il naît 105 garçons.

L’âge conjoncturel moyen à l’accouchement est un âge calculé pour une génération fictive de femmes qui auraient à chaque âge
                           la fécondité observée pour les femmes du même âge l’année considérée.

L’espérance de vie à la naissance est égale à la durée de vie moyenne d’une génération fictive qui connaîtrait tout
                           au long de son existence les conditions de mortalité par âge de l’année considérée.
                           C’est un indicateur synthétique des taux de mortalité par âge de l’année considérée.

## Définitions

Le terme générique de « populations de référence » regroupe pour chaque commune sa
                        population municipale, sa population comptée à part et sa population totale qui est
                        la somme des deux précédentes.
Les populations de référence sont définies par le décret n°2003-485 publié au Journal
                        officiel du 8 juin 2003, relatif au recensement de la population, modifié par le décret
                        n° 2019-1302 du 5 décembre 2019. Désormais, elles sont actualisées et authentifiées
                        par un décret chaque année. Environ 350 textes législatifs ou réglementaires font
                        référence à ces populations.
La population municipale est celle qui est utilisée à des fins statistiques ; la population
                        totale est la plus souvent utilisée pour l'application de dispositions législatives
                        ou réglementaires.

## Définitions

Toutes les définitions des concepts utilisés sont accessibles dans la [rubrique définitions](/fr/metadonnees/definitions)
Concernant spécifiquement le recensement de la population, se référer à [la définition des concepts du recensement de la population](/fr/information/2383278)

## Champ

### Recensements de la population

Les données sont proposées aux utilisateurs notamment pour
                     comparer des communes, regrouper des modalités de variables ou obtenir
                     des résultats sur des ensembles personnalisés de communes.
Issues de calculs liés aux techniques d’échantillonnage, les
                     données en effectifs sont fournies avec plusieurs décimales ; celles-ci
                     doivent être utilisées pour tous les calculs réalisés, de façon à éviter
                     les erreurs d’arrondis.
Pour avoir plus d’information sur le recensement de la
                     population, consultez la page de [présentation du recensement de la
                        population](/fr/information/2383265).
Les données proviennent soit de l’exploitation principale
                     (princ), soit de l’exploitation complémentaire (compl).
Pour plus d’information méthodologique, vous pouvez consulter
                     les fiches ["Conseils pour
                        l’utilisation des résultats du recensement"](/fr/information/2383177).
Ces fiches présentent les caractéristiques du recensement de la
                     population et traitent de leurs conséquences sur l’utilisation des
                     données. Elles précisent en particulier les changements affectant les
                     principales variables statistiques et leur comparabilité avec les
                     recensements précédents.

### État civil

Les statistiques annuelles concernant les naissances
                     domiciliées sont dressées à partir des bulletins
                     statistiques de l’état civil, établis par les maires, au moment et dans
                     la commune où ont lieu les naissances. Elles portent sur les naissances
                     ayant eu lieu dans toutes les communes de France. Les naissances ayant
                     eu lieu à l’étranger ou dans les COM ne sont pas comptabilisées.
La variable "commune" correspond à la commune du domicile de la
                     mère en France.
Les statistiques comprennent les jugements déclaratifs de
                     naissance, mais ne prennent pas en compte les enfants mort-nés.

Les statistiques annuelles concernant les décès
                     domiciliés sont dressées à partir des bulletins
                     statistiques de l’état civil, établis par les maires, au moment et dans
                     la commune où ont lieu les décès. Elles portent sur les décès ayant eu
                     lieu dans toutes les communes de France. Les décès ayant eu lieu à
                     l’étranger ou dans les COM ne sont pas comptabilisés.
La variable "commune" correspond à la commune du domicile du
                     défunt en France.
Les statistiques comprennent les jugements déclaratifs de décès.

### Fichier Localisé Social et Fiscal (Filosofi)

Le champ porte sur les personnes appartenant à des ménages
                     fiscaux ordinaires dont le revenu disponible est positif ou nul.
Les résultats couvrent la France métropolitaine et La Réunion.

### Base Tous Salariés (BTS)

Le champ correspond aux salariés du privé, y compris alternants,
                     stagiaires et bénéficiaires de contrats aidés, hors salariés de l’agriculture
                     et des particuliers employeurs.

### Système d’information sur la démographie d’entreprises (Side)

Les indicateurs portent sur les créations et les stocks
                     d’entreprises et d’établissements de l’ensemble des activités
                     productives et marchandes non agricoles. Ce champ inclut les activités
                     financières.
Quand on parle d’entreprises, tous les dénombrements portent en
                     réalité sur des unités légales pour cette source. Lorsqu’une unité
                     légale comprend plusieurs établissements, elle est localisée à son
                     siège.
Le nombre de créations d’entreprises ou d’établissements
                     correspond au nombre d’unités légales ou d’établissements créés au cours
                     de l’année N.
Le nombre d’entreprises ou d’établissements de l’année N
                     correspond au nombre d’unités légales ou d’établissements économiquement
                     actifs en N.

### Fichier localisé des rémunérations et de l’emploi salarié (Flores)

Le dispositif Flores (Fichier localisé des rémunérations et de
                     l’emploi salarié) couvre les établissements ayant employé au moins un
                     salarié pendant l’année, en France. Dans cette base
                     communale, les données mises à disposition sont par ailleurs restreintes
                     aux établissements actifs en fin d’année (dernière semaine de décembre),
                     ce qui exclut les établissements qui ont cessé leur activité en cours
                     d’année.
L’effectif salarié en fin d’année correspond au nombre de postes
                     présents la dernière semaine de décembre dans l’établissement employeur.
                     L’effectif en fin d’année de certains établissements peut donc être nul,
                     si le ou les personnes salariées pendant l’année n’étaient plus en
                     emploi fin décembre.
Flores couvre l’ensemble de l’emploi salarié, quel que soit le
                     secteur d’activité et le type d’employeur (public ou privé, y compris
                     les particuliers employeurs). Sont exclus du champ les établissements
                     relevant du ministère des Armées (personnels militaires comme civils).

### Base permanente des équipements (BPE)

La base permanente des équipements (BPE) est une base à vocation
                     statistique. Elle répertorie un large éventail d’équipements et de
                     services, marchands ou non, accessibles au public sur l’ensemble de la
                     France au 1ᵉʳ janvier de chaque année.
La base permanente des équipements (BPE) est un dispositif
                     alimenté par différentes sources : [sources
                        utilisées par la BPE](/fr/metadonnees/source/operation/s2216/processus-statistique).

### Tourisme

Le champ porte sur les hôtels de tourisme, classés ou pas, de
                     plus de 5
                     chambres et sur les campings de plus de 10 emplacements, classés ou pas,
                     y compris les
                     campings résidentiels. Il porte également sur les autres hébergements
                     collectifs
                     touristiques.
Les statistiques sur l’offre d’hébergements sont établies en
                     relation avec
                     les comités régionaux de tourisme (CRT). Elles sont proposées au niveau
                     communal pour
                     la France (hors Mayotte).
Les statistiques concernant l’hôtellerie de plein air portent
                     sur les
                     campings offrant des emplacements à la clientèle de passage destinés aux
                     touristes n’y
                     élisant pas domicile ainsi que sur les campings proposant des
                     emplacements loués à
                     l’année, c’est à-dire à un seul client pour l’ensemble de la période
                     d’ouverture du
                     camping.
Les hôtels et les campings classés le sont selon la nouvelle
                     nomenclature de
                     classification mise en œuvre par l’opérateur Atout France.

### Répertoire électoral unique

Le Répertoire électoral unique couvre l’ensemble des territoires
                     français à l’exception de la Nouvelle-Calédonie.
Le champ porte sur les électeurs inscrits sur la liste
                     électorale principale.
Les listes électorales principales, tenues par les communes,
                     recensent les électeurs français qui leur sont rattachés et qui sont
                     admis à participer aux scrutins relevant des dispositions du Code
                     électoral, et à toute autre consultation établie sur la base de ces
                     listes.

A financial crisis and social distress led in May 1789 to the [convocation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convocation) of the [Estates General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estates_General_of_1789), which was converted into a [National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_(French_Revolution)) in June. The [Storming of the Bastille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storming_of_the_Bastille) on 14 July led to a series of radical measures by the Assembly, among them the [abolition of feudalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolition_of_feudalism_in_France), state control over the [Catholic Church in France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_France), and a [declaration of rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen).[[58]](#cite_note-69)
The next three years were dominated by a struggle for political control, exacerbated by [economic depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_depression). Military defeats following the outbreak of the [French Revolutionary Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolutionary_Wars) in April 1792 resulted in the [insurrection of 10 August 1792](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insurrection_of_10_August_1792). The [monarchy was abolished](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_abolition_of_the_monarchy) and replaced by the [French First Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_First_Republic) in September, while [Louis XVI was executed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_of_Louis_XVI) in January 1793.[[59]](#cite_note-70)
After another [revolt in June 1793](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insurrection_of_31_May_–_2_June_1793), the constitution was suspended and power passed from the [National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Convention) to the [Committee of Public Safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_of_Public_Safety). About 16,000 people were executed in a [Reign of Terror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reign_of_Terror), which [ended in July 1794](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermidorian_Reaction). Weakened by external threats and internal opposition, the Republic was replaced in 1795 by the [Directory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Directory). In 1799, the [Consulate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Consulate) seized power in [a coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_of_18_Brumaire) led by [Napoleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon).[[60]](#cite_note-71)

### Napoleonic France (1799–1815)

Main article: [France in the long nineteenth century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_in_the_long_nineteenth_century)[Napoleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon), [Emperor of the French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_of_the_French), built [a vast empire across Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_French_Empire).[[61]](#cite_note-72)
[Napoleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon) became [First Consul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Consulate) in 1799 and later [Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_Year_XII) of the [French Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_French_Empire). Changing sets of [European coalitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolutionary_and_Napoleonic_Wars) declared [wars on Napoleon's empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars). His armies conquered most of continental Europe with swift victories such as the [Austerlitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Austerlitz), [Jena-Auerstadt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Jena–Auerstedt) and [Battle of Friedland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Friedland). Members of the [Bonaparte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Bonaparte) family were appointed monarchs in some of the newly established kingdoms.[[62]](#cite_note-Blanning-73)
These victories led to the worldwide expansion of French revolutionary ideals and reforms, such as the [metric system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_system), [Napoleonic Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Code) and [Declaration of the Rights of Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen). In 1812 Napoleon [attacked Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_invasion_of_Russia), reaching [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow). Thereafter his army disintegrated through supply problems, disease, Russian attacks, and finally winter. After this catastrophic campaign and the ensuing [uprising of European monarchies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Sixth_Coalition) against his rule, Napoleon was defeated. About 306,000 to a million Frenchmen [died during the Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars_casualties).[[47]](#cite_note-c-58)[[62]](#cite_note-Blanning-73) After his [brief return](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hundred_Days) from exile, Napoleon was finally defeated in 1815 at the [Battle of Waterloo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Waterloo), and the [Bourbon monarchy was restored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_Restoration_in_France) with new constitutional limitations.

### Colonial empire

The discredited Bourbon dynasty was overthrown by the [July Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_Revolution) of 1830, which established the constitutional [July Monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_Monarchy); French troops began the [conquest of Algeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_conquest_of_Algeria). Unrest led to the [French Revolution of 1848](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution_of_1848) and the end of the July Monarchy. The abolition of slavery and the introduction of male universal suffrage was re-enacted in 1848. In 1852, president of the French Republic, [Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon_III), Napoleon I's nephew, was proclaimed emperor of the [Second Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_French_Empire), as Napoleon III. He multiplied French interventions abroad, especially in [Crimea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_War), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_French_intervention_in_Mexico) and [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Italian_War_of_Independence). Napoleon III was unseated following defeat in the [Franco-Prussian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco-Prussian_War) of 1870, and his regime was replaced by the [Third Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Third_Republic). By 1875, the French conquest of Algeria was complete, with approximately 825,000 Algerians killed from famine, disease, and violence.[[63]](#cite_note-Kiernan2007-74) France suffered an estimated 10,000 killed and 35,000 wounded across all colonial campaigns.[[47]](#cite_note-c-58) A few thousand died in Mexico or [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_conquest_of_Vietnam), but the vast majority perished in Algeria. Disease claimed an even heavier toll; one estimate puts total French and [Foreign Legion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Foreign_Legion) deaths from battle and disease for the entire 19th century at 110,000.[[47]](#cite_note-c-58)[French colonial empires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_colonial_empire):
  First
  Second
France had [colonial possessions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_colonial_empire) since the beginning of the 17th century, but in the 19th and 20th centuries its empire extended significantly and became [the second-largest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires) behind the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire).[[64]](#cite_note-Lexington_Books-2005-75) Including metropolitan France, the total area reached almost 13 million square kilometres in the 1920s and 1930s, 9% of the world's land. Known as the [Belle Époque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belle_Époque), the turn of the century was characterised by optimism, regional peace, economic prosperity and technological, scientific and cultural innovations. In 1905, [state secularism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secular_state) was [officially established](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1905_French_law_on_the_Separation_of_the_Churches_and_the_State).[[65]](#cite_note-76)

### Early to mid-20th century (1914–1946)

Main article: [History of France (1900–present)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_France_(1900–present))French [Poilus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poilu) posing with their war-torn flag in 1917, during World War I
During World War I, France played a [decisive role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Army_in_World_War_I) in defeating the [Central Powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Powers) as part of the [Triple Entente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_Entente), while participating in the majority of the war's major battles fought on the Western Front.[[66]](#cite_note-77) A rich industrial area in the north was occupied. France and the [Allies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_I) emerged victorious against the [Central Powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Powers) at tremendous human cost. It left 1.4 million French soldiers dead, 4% of its population.[[67]](#cite_note-78)[[68]](#cite_note-79) In addition, France suffered 4,266,000 wounded.[[47]](#cite_note-c-58) Interwar was marked by [intense international tensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Events_preceding_World_War_II_in_Europe) and social reforms introduced by the [Popular Front government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Front_(France)) (e.g., [annual leave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annual_leave), [eight-hour workdays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight-hour_day), [women in government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_government)).
In 1940, France was [invaded and quickly defeated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France) by [Nazi Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany). France was divided into a [German occupation zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_military_administration_in_occupied_France_during_World_War_II) in the north, an [Italian occupation zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_occupation_of_France) and an unoccupied territory, the rest of France, which consisted of southern France and the French empire. The [Vichy government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vichy_France), an authoritarian regime collaborating with Germany, ruled the unoccupied territory. [Free France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_France), the government-in-exile led by [Charles de Gaulle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_de_Gaulle), was set up in London.[[69]](#cite_note-80)
From 1942 to 1944, about 160,000 French citizens, including around [75,000 Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_France),[[70]](#cite_note-81) were deported to [death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extermination_camp) and [concentration camps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internment).[[71]](#cite_note-82) On 6 June 1944, the Allies [invaded Normandy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Overlord), and in August they [invaded Provence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Dragoon). The Allies and [French Resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Resistance) emerged victorious, and French sovereignty was restored with the [Provisional Government of the French Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provisional_Government_of_the_French_Republic) (GPRF). This interim government, established by de Gaulle, continued to [wage war against Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Allied_invasion_of_Germany) and to [purge collaborators from office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Épuration_légale). It made important reforms e.g. suffrage extended to women and the creation of a [social security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_security_in_France) system.

### 1946–present
[Charles de Gaulle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_de_Gaulle), a hero of World War I, leader of the [Free French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_French_Forces) during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II), and [President of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France)
A new constitution resulted in the [Fourth Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Fourth_Republic) (1946–1958), which saw strong economic growth (les [Trente Glorieuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trente_Glorieuses)). France was a founding member of [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO) and attempted to [regain control of French Indochina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Indochina_War), but was defeated by the [Viet Minh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viet_Minh) in 1954. France faced another [anti-colonialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-colonialist) [conflict in Algeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algerian_War), then part of France and home to over one million European settlers ([Pied-Noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pied-Noir)). The French systematically used torture and repression, including extrajudicial killings to keep control.[[72]](#cite_note-Macqueen2014-83) This conflict nearly led to a coup and civil war.[[73]](#cite_note-84)
During the [May 1958 crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_1958_crisis_in_France), the weak Fourth Republic gave way to the [Fifth Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Fifth_Republic), which included a strengthened presidency.[[74]](#cite_note-85) The war concluded with the [Évian Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Évian_Accords) in 1962 which led to [Algerian independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_Algerian_independence_referendum), at a high price: between half a million and one million deaths and over 2 million internally-displaced Algerians.[[75]](#cite_note-Springer-86) Around one million Pied-Noirs and [Harkis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harki) fled from Algeria to France.[[76]](#cite_note-google4-87) A vestige of the empire is the [French overseas departments and territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_France).
During the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War), de Gaulle pursued a policy of "national independence" towards the [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Bloc) and [Eastern blocs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bloc). He withdrew from NATO's military-integrated command (while remaining within the alliance), launched a [nuclear development programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_de_dissuasion) and made France the [fourth nuclear power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction). He [restored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Élysée_Treaty) cordial [Franco-German relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France–Germany_relations) to create a European counterweight between American and Soviet spheres of influence. However, he opposed any development of a [supranational Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supranational_union), favouring [sovereign nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state). The revolt of [May 1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_68) had an enormous social impact; it was a watershed moment when a conservative moral ideal (religion, patriotism, respect for authority) shifted to a more liberal moral ideal (secularism, individualism, sexual revolution). Although the revolt was a political failure (the [Gaullist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaullism) party emerged stronger than before) it announced a split between the French and de Gaulle, who resigned.[[77]](#cite_note-88)
In the post-Gaullist era, France remained one of the most developed [economies in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)) but faced crises that resulted in high unemployment rates and increasing public debt. In the late 20th and early 21st centuries, France has been at the forefront of the development of a supranational [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union), notably by signing the [Maastricht Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty) in 1992, establishing the [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone) in 1999[[78]](#cite_note-superficy-89) and signing the [Treaty of Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon) in 2007.[[79]](#cite_note-90) France has fully reintegrated into NATO and since participated in most NATO-sponsored wars.[[80]](#cite_note-91)[Calais Jungle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calais_Jungle)
Since the 19th century, France has [received many immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_France), often male [foreign workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_worker) from European Catholic countries who generally returned home when not employed.[[81]](#cite_note-Marie-Christine_Weidmann-Koop-92) During the 1970s, France faced an economic crisis and allowed new immigrants (mostly from the [Maghreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maghreb), in northwest Africa)[[81]](#cite_note-Marie-Christine_Weidmann-Koop-92) to permanently [settle in France with their families](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_reunification) and acquire citizenship. It resulted in hundreds of thousands of Muslims living in subsidised public housing and suffering from high unemployment rates.[[82]](#cite_note-93) The government had a policy of [assimilation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_assimilation) of immigrants, where they were expected to adhere to French values and norms.[[83]](#cite_note-94) From the 2000s, France experienced continued immigration from Africa, the Middle East, and Asia. The Île-de-France ([/ˌiːl də ˈfrɒ̃s/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English); French: [[il də fʁɑ̃s]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French) [ⓘ](/wiki/File:LL-Q150_(fra)-WikiLucas00-%C3%8Ele-de-France.wav); lit.'Island of France') is the most populous of the eighteen [regions of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_France), with an official estimated population of 12,271,794 residents on 1 January 2023.[[1]](#cite_note-pop2022-1) Containing the capital city of France, [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris), it is located in the north-central part of the country and often called the Paris Region[[3]](#cite_note-iledefrance.fr_Essentials2018-3) (French: Région parisienne, pronounced [[ʁeʒjɔ̃ paʁizjɛn]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French)). Île-de-France is densely populated and retains a prime economic position on the national stage. It covers 12,012 square kilometres (4,638 square miles), about 2% of [metropolitan French territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_France). Its 2017 population was nearly one-fifth of the national total.[[4]](#cite_note-auto1-4)
The region is made up of eight administrative [departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_France): Paris, [Essonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essonne), [Hauts-de-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hauts-de-Seine), [Seine-Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-Saint-Denis), [Seine-et-Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-et-Marne), [Val-de-Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-de-Marne), [Val-d'Oise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-d'Oise) and [Yvelines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yvelines). It was created as the "District of the Paris Region" in 1961. In 1976, when its status was aligned with the French administrative regions created in 1972, it was renamed after the historic province of Île-de-France. Residents are sometimes referred to as Franciliens, an administrative word created in the 1980s. The GDP of the region in 2019 was nearly one-third of the total for France,[[5]](#cite_note-cci_paris2022-5):12 and 5% of the European Union's.[[5]](#cite_note-cci_paris2022-5):12 It has the highest per capita GDP of any French region.[[6]](#cite_note-oecdatlas-6)
Beyond the city limits of Paris, the region has many other important historic sites, including the palaces of [Versailles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Versailles) and [Fontainebleau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Fontainebleau), as well as the most-visited tourist attraction in France, [Disneyland Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disneyland_Paris). Although it is the richest French region, a significant number of residents live in poverty. The official poverty rate in the Île-de-France was 15.9% in 2015. The region has witnessed increasing income inequality in recent decades, and rising housing prices have pushed the less affluent outside Paris.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

## Etymology
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%8Ele-de-France&action=edit&section=1)]
Further information: [History of Île-de-France § Early history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Île-de-France#Early_history)
Although the modern name Île-de-France literally means Island of France, its etymology is unclear. Despite its name, the region itself is not an island. The "island" may refer to the land between the rivers [Oise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oise_(river)), [Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marne_(river)) and [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine), or it may also have been a reference to the [Île de la Cité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île_de_la_Cité), where the French royal palace and cathedral were located.[[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]
Alternatively, the name may refer to the [lands that were under the direct rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_lands_of_France) of the [Capetian kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capetian_dynasty) during the [Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages); thus, the lands were an "island" in a sea of various [feudal territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feudalism) ruled by [vassals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vassal) of the king.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

## History
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%8Ele-de-France&action=edit&section=2)]
Main article: [History of Île-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Île-de-France)Historic extent of the Île-de-France
The Île-de-France was inhabited by the [Parisii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parisii_(Gaul)), a sub-tribe of the [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celt) [Senones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senones), from around the middle of the 3rd-century BC.[[9]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEArbois_de_JubainvilleDottin1889132-9)[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECunliffe2004201-10) One of the area's major north–south trade routes crossed the Seine on the [île de la Cité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Île_de_la_Cité); the meeting place of land and water trade routes gradually became an important trading centre.[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELawrenceGondrand201025-11) The Parisii traded with many river towns (some as far away as the Iberian Peninsula) and minted their own coins for that purpose.[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmidt200965–70-12)
The [Romans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome) conquered the area in 52 BC and began their settlement on Paris's [Left Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rive_Gauche).[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmidt200988–104-13) It became a prosperous city with a forum, baths, temples, theatres, and an amphitheatre.[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmidt2009154–167-14) [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity) was introduced in the middle of the 3rd century AD by [Saint Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Denis_of_Paris), the first Bishop of Paris. According to legend, when Denis refused to renounce his faith before Roman authorities, he was beheaded on the hill that became known as Mons Martyrum (Latin "Hill of Martyrs"), later "[Montmartre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montmartre)". The legend further states that Denis walked headless from this hill to the north of the city. The place that he finally fell and was buried became an important religious shrine, the [Basilica of Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_Saint-Denis).[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmidt2009210–11-15)
[Clovis the Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clovis_the_Frank), the first king of the [Merovingian dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merovingian_dynasty), made the city his capital in 508. As the Frankish domination of Gaul began, there was a gradual immigration by the [Franks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franks) to Paris and the Parisian [Francien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francien_language) dialects were born. Fortification of the Île de la Cité failed to avert [sacking by Vikings in 845](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Paris_(845)), but Paris's strategic importance—with its bridges preventing ships from passing—was established by successful defence in the [Siege of Paris (885–86)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Paris_(885–86)). In 987, [Hugh Capet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Capet), [Count of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Count_of_Paris) (comte de Paris) and [Duke of the Franks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_of_the_Franks) (duc des Francs), was elected [King of the Franks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_French_monarchs) (roi des Francs). Under the rule of the [Capetian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Capet) kings, Paris gradually became the largest and most prosperous city in France.[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmidt2009210–11-15)
The Kings of France enjoyed getting away from Paris and hunting in the game-filled forests of the region. They built palatial hunting lodges, most notably [Palace of Fontainebleau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Fontainebleau) and the [Palace of Versailles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Versailles). From the time of Louis XIV to the French Revolution, Versailles was the official residence of the Kings and the seat of the French government. Île-de-France became the term used for the territory of Paris and the surrounding province, which was administered directly by the King.[[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]
During the [French Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution), the royal provinces were abolished and divided into departments, and the city and region were governed directly by the national government. After World War II, as Paris faced a major housing shortage, hundreds of massive apartment blocks for low-income residents were built around the edges of Paris. In the 1950s and the 1960s, thousands of immigrants settled in the communes bordering the city. In 1959, under President [Charles De Gaulle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_De_Gaulle), a new region was created out of six departments, which corresponded approximately with the historic region, with the name District de la région de Paris ("District of the Paris Region"). On 6 May 1976, as part of the process of [regionalisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regionalism_(politics)), the district was reconstituted with increased administrative and political powers and renamed the Île-de-France region.[[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]

## Geography
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%8Ele-de-France&action=edit&section=3)]
Île-de-France is in the north of France, neighboring [Hauts-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hauts-de-France) to the north, [Grand Est](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Est) to the east, [Bourgogne-Franche-Comté](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourgogne-Franche-Comté) to the southeast, [Centre-Val-de-Loire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre-Val_de_Loire) to the southwest, and [Normandy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normandy) to the west.

### Departments
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%8Ele-de-France&action=edit&section=4)]
Île-de-France has a land area of 12,011 km2 (4,637 sq mi). It is composed of eight [departments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_France) centred on its innermost department and capital, Paris. Around the department and municipality of Paris, urbanisation fills a first concentric ring of three departments commonly known as the petite couronne ("small ring"); it extends into a second outer ring of four departments known as the grande couronne ("large ring"). The [former department of Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine_(department)), abolished in 1968, included the city proper and parts of the petite couronne.
The petite couronne consists of the departments of [Hauts-de-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hauts-de-Seine), [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris), [Seine-Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-Saint-Denis) and [Val-de-Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-de-Marne); the grande couronne consists of those of [Seine-et-Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-et-Marne), [Yvelines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yvelines), [Essonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essonne) and [Val-d'Oise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-d'Oise). Politically, the region is divided into 8 departments, 25 arrondissements, 155 cantons and 1,276 communes, out of the total of 35,416 in [metropolitan France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_France).[[4]](#cite_note-auto1-4)

### Topography
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%8Ele-de-France&action=edit&section=5)]
The outer parts of the Île-de-France remain largely rural. Agricultural land, forest and natural spaces occupy 78.9 percent of the region, and 28 percent of the region's land is in urban use.[[17]](#cite_note-17)
The River [Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine) flows through the middle of the region, which is crisscrossed by its tributaries and sub-tributaries, including the Rivers [Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marne_(river)), [Oise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oise_(river)) and [Epte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epte). The River [Eure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eure_(river)) does not cross the region but receives water from several rivers in the Île-de-France, including the Drouette and the Vesgre. The major rivers are navigable, and, because of the modest variations of altitude in the region (between 10 metres (33 ft) and 200 metres (660 ft)), they have a tendency to meander and curve. They also create many lakes and ponds, some of which have been transformed into recreation areas, including Moisson-Mousseaux, Cergy-Neuville and [Villeneuve-Saint-Georges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villeneuve-Saint-Georges).

## Economy
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%8Ele-de-France&action=edit&section=6)]Paris as an engine of the global economy: the skyscrapers of [La Défense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Défense), the largest purpose-built business district of Europe, with 3.35 million m² (36 million sq. ft) of office space.[[18]](#cite_note-18)
Île-de-France produced €742 billion ([gross domestic product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product))[[5]](#cite_note-cci_paris2022-5) or around 1/3 of the [economy of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_France) in 2019.[[5]](#cite_note-cci_paris2022-5):12 The regional economy has gradually shifted toward high-value-added service industries (finance, IT services etc.) and high-tech manufacturing (electronics, optics, aerospace etc.).[[19]](#cite_note-INSEE_201210-19) In 2014, industry represented just under five percent of active enterprises in the region, and 10.2 percent of salaried workers. Commerce and services account for 84 percent of the business establishments in the region, and have 83.3 percent of the salaried employees.[[20]](#cite_note-20) Financial services and insurance are important sectors of the regional economy; the major French banks and insurance companies, including [BNP Paribas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BNP_Paribas), [Société Générale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Société_Générale) and [Crédit Agricole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crédit_Agricole), all have their headquarters in the region. The region also hosts the headquarters of the top French telecom companies and utilities, including [Orange S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_S.A.), [Veolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veolia) and [EDF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Électricité_de_France). The French stock market, the [Bourse de Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourse_de_Paris), now known as [Euronext Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euronext_Paris), occupies a historical building in the center of Paris and is ranked fourth among global stock markets, after New York, Tokyo and London.[[21]](#cite_note-auto3-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22) Other major sectors of the regional economy include energy companies ([Orano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orano), [Engie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engie), [Électricité de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Électricité_de_France) and [Total S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_S.A.)). The two major French automobile manufacturers, [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault), in [Flins-sur-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flins-sur-Seine), and [Groupe PSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groupe_PSA), in [Poissy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poissy), do much of their assembly work outside France but still have research centre and large plants in the region. The leading French and European aerospace and defense companies, including [Airbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus), [Thales Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thales_Group), [Dassault Aviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Aviation), [Safran Aircraft Engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safran_Aircraft_Engines), the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency), [Alcatel-Lucent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcatel-Lucent), and [Arianespace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianespace), have a large presence in the region.[[21]](#cite_note-auto3-21)
The region is served by [Charles de Gaulle Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_de_Gaulle_Airport). The airport is also the hub of [Air France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_France). In 2024, the airport handled 70,290,260 passengers and 466,543 aircraft movements, making it the [world's fourteenth busiest airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_busiest_airports_by_passenger_traffic) and [Europe's third busiest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_Europe) airport (after [Heathrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heathrow_Airport) and [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul_Airport)) in terms of passenger numbers.[[23]](#cite_note-:1-23) Charles de Gaulle is the busiest airport within the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union). In terms of cargo traffic, the airport is the second busiest in Europe, after [Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_Airport), handling 1,914,681 tonnes of cargo in 2024.[[23]](#cite_note-:1-23) As of 2025, it was the airport served by the second highest number of [airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airlines), after [Suvarnabhumi Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suvarnabhumi_Airport), with 105 airlines operating from it.[[24]](#cite_note-24) [Orly Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orly_Airport) also remains the busiest French airport for domestic traffic and the [second busiest French airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_France) overall in passenger traffic, with 33,123,027 passengers in 2024.
The energy sector is also well established in the region. The nuclear power industry, with its major firm being [Orano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orano), has its headquarters in Île-de-France, as does the main French oil company [Total S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_S.A.), the top French company in the Fortune Global 500, and the main electric utility, [Électricité de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Électricité_de_France). The energy firm [Engie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engie) also has its main offices in the region at [La Défense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Défense).

### Employment
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%8Ele-de-France&action=edit&section=7)]
In 2018 just 7.2 percent of employees in the region were engaged in industry; 62.3 percent were engaged in commerce and market services; 25.5 percent in non-market services, including government, health and education; 4.8 percent in construction; and 0.2 percent in agriculture.[[25]](#cite_note-auto-25)
The largest non-government employers in the region as of the end of 2015 were the airline [Air France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_France) (40,657); the [SNCF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNCF) (French Railways, 31,955); the telecom firm [Orange S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_S.A.) (31,497); the bank [Société Générale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Société_Générale) (27,361); the automotive firm [Groupe PSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groupe_PSA) (19,648); [EDF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Électricité_de_France) (Electricité de France, 18,199); and [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault) (18,136).[[26]](#cite_note-cci_paris2018_a-26) While the Petite Couronne, or departments closest to Paris, previously employed the most industrial workers, the largest number is now in the Grande Couronne, the outer departments.[[25]](#cite_note-auto-25)
The unemployment rate in the region stood at 8.6% at the end of 2016. It varied within the region from 7.8 percent in the city of Paris, to a high of 12.7 percent in [Seine-Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine-Saint-Denis), and 10 percent in [Val-d'Oise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-d'Oise); to regional lows of 7.4 percent in [Yvelines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yvelines); 7.5 percent in [Hauts-de-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hauts-de-Seine); 7.7 percent in [Essonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essonne); 7.9 percent in [Seine et Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine_et_Marne), and 8.8 percent in [Val de Marne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val_de_Marne).[[27]](#cite_note-27)

### Agriculture
[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C3%8Ele-de-France&action=edit&section=8)]
In 2018, 48 percent of the land of the Île-de-France was devoted to agriculture; 569,000 hectares were cultivated. The most important crops are grains (66 percent), followed by beets (7 percent), largely for industrial use, and grass for grazing. In 2014, 9,495 hectares were devoted to bio-agriculture. However, the number of persons employed in agriculture in the region dropped 33 percent between 2000 and 2015 to just 8,460 persons in 2015.[[28]](#cite_note-28)
